source.title: Training Trajectories Determine Circuit Removability in Annealable Soft-Prior Transformers
source.authors: Zong-Lin Yang; Zi-Ming Zhao; Wei Tang; Xun-Yu Jiang; Yi-Hong Liu; Tai-Lin Chen; Zi-Fu Yu; Jia-Yu Liu

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how training path and task affect whether small synthetic retrieval circuits remain functional after removing a positional prior; it refines the scope of claims about induction and in-context learning rather than reproducing the original measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper measures task accuracy and head-level successor-value mass and ablation importance. It does not test previous-token-head composition, loss by token index, or the training-loss bump. Static positional-encoding comparisons are omitted because they do not test induction-head formation or removability. The schedule-shape text gives an aggregate range for linear, cosine, and convex schedules; individual values in the flattened figure are not used where they conflict with that text.
record.test_reason: In small soft-prior Transformers, the study reports whether retrieval and induction-task in-context performance forms and persists without the prior, depending on the training path (gate schedule). This is a training-setup dependence, so it is a new-setting result for V5. It does not identify induction heads by the original prefix-matching or copying tests, does not measure previous-token composition or loss by token index, and argues no version wrong, so T3 rather than T5. Its head-level traces only weakly bear on V4 and cannot resolve V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that for small discrete retrieval tasks, whether a positional prior can be removed depends on the training trajectory. Smooth fade-to-zero works, while unforced, forced-zero, hard-switch and post-hoc paths do not. Mechanism traces place consolidation after the gate reaches zero, with head identity varying by seed. Linear regression ICL is a boundary case where zero-gate training succeeds directly.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gated positional and content biases with scheduled gate removal, task accuracy, successor-value mass, and head ablation. It does not use the original induction-head identification, previous-token-head composition, or loss-by-token-index measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes with gate schedule and fade shape, fade start, task (associative recall and Markov induction versus linear regression ICL), and model size. The text reports concave-schedule instability and weak length extrapolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Head identity of the retrieval circuit varies across seeds (L1H0, L1H3, L1H1), while threshold-crossing timing is identical across seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The timing of retrieval-circuit consolidation is seed-stable even when the identity of the head carrying it varies.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to synthetic tasks and Transformers no larger than L=4 and d=128. Head-level traces cover three seeds of the base model; the responsible heads vary. Several Markov-path comparisons are shown only in a figure, and the study does not measure the specific previous-token composition or token-index loss behavior in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted static-baseline comparisons and length-generalization accuracy because they do not test induction-head formation or prior-free persistence as specified. Figure-only individual schedule-shape values were not assigned where the extracted figure values conflict with the text's schedule summary.

untested.parts: Composition with a previous-token head and the [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying mechanism are not tested.
No loss bump, no token-index in-context-learning score, and no test of abrupt co-occurrence.
No large models and no token-index loss.
Only three seeds of one tiny custom soft-prior architecture (L=2, d=64). No other families, sizes, modalities, or head traces for the larger model.
Two metrics with arbitrary thresholds sampled every 300 steps cannot show whether formation is several transitions or one. The authors make no such claim.

missing.what: Static positional-encoding comparison: whether associative recall and Markov induction are learned at all depends on the positional scheme (soft bias ~0.79; RoPE, NoPE, vanilla, GPSA near chance). This is relevant to V5 as setup dependence.
Gate intervention on an unforced model: zeroing the positional gate collapses accuracy from 0.794 to 0.073, while zeroing the content gate leaves it at 0.791.
Five-seed unforced (.095 ± .009) and forced_zero (.091 ± .012) zero-gate controls.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 'supports' is withdrawn. Different metrics crossing arbitrary thresholds 300 steps apart do not show a multi-transition formation, and the authors do not claim one. The reader's V4 'limits_scope' for untested families is moved to untested. The contributions list mentions prior dropout and a dual condition loss, but the text reports no results for them. The model is a custom soft-prior architecture, so its link to standard induction-head formation is indirect.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test composition with an earlier previous-token head or the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying mechanism.
Does not measure induction-head formation against loss by token index or a training-loss bump, or establish a narrow early-training phase change.
Does not test whether induction heads carry most in-context learning in large transformers; models are small synthetic-task models and no token-index loss measure is reported.
Head-level diagnostics cover three seeds of the base model, not other model families, modalities, or architectures; the larger model is not given the same head-level trace.
Tests positional-prior schedules and a small set of synthetic tasks, not general training-data properties or broad training setups.
Does not compare few-shot task learning against other heads or mechanisms as carriers.
Tests two mechanistic indicators with separate thresholds, not whether all induction-head formation consists of multiple distinct transitions.

relationships.condition: Associative recall and Markov induction, L=2 and L=4 soft-prior Transformers
relationships.reason: Zero-gate retrieval forms with gradual fade (.73–.75; Markov .83–.97). It fails under unforced, forced-zero, hard-switch and post-hoc paths (~.09–.29). Measure is task accuracy, not identified induction heads. Rows r1,r4,r5,r6,r9,r10,r11,r12,r14,r15,r19–r27.
relationships.display_finding: Gradual fading produced zero-gate retrieval accuracies of 0.73–0.75 for associative recall and 0.83–0.97 for Markov induction, compared with approximately 0.09–0.29 under alternative training paths.

source_check.condition: Associative recall and Markov induction, L=2 and L=4 soft-prior Transformers
source_check.reason: Retrieval persistence depends on training path. The L=4 capacity comparison and hard-switch/post-hoc controls concern associative recall; Markov induction supplies a separate task comparison.

relationships.reason: Forced-zero learns the task directly (0.0722 MSE) and fade is only slightly better (0.0646), so path dependence is weak for this task (r28–r30).
relationships.display_finding: Training with gates forced to zero learned linear regression directly with MSE 0.0722, while gradual fading improved it only slightly to 0.0646.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: V5 asserts dependence on task properties and training setup, not universal necessity of fading. Forced-zero learning and the smaller fade advantage establish task dependence, while unforced zero-gate degradation still demonstrates setup dependence.

relationships.condition: Three seeds of the base fade600→0 soft-prior model only
relationships.reason: A layer-1 head with successor-value mass ≥.25 appears in every seed, though in a different head each time (r31, r33, r35). This is thin evidence: one tiny architecture.
relationships.display_finding: Every seed develops a layer-1 head with successor-value mass at least 0.25, with a different head selected each time.

relation.reason: Controlled training paths and zero-gate evaluations directly test training-setup dependence under V5; seeded head diagnostics also bear narrowly on V4.

tranche.reason: Gated soft-prior Transformers provide a new setting testing how training paths affect persistence of retrieval-task ICL.

source_check.notes: Normal-evaluation baselines for scheduled runs are genuine diagnostic cells; zero-gate training-path controls are needed to assess fade efficacy. Successor-value mass supports a narrow behavioral head claim, without identifying previous-token composition or establishing multiple phase transitions.

statements.correction: Linear-regression MSE: unforced normal=0.0656; unforced zero-gate=0.1296; forced-zero=0.0722; fade=0.0646. Gradual fading is less necessary for this task. Task-dependent training-path effects support V5.
statements.problem: The task comparison and numbers are correct, but the limits_scope placement qualifies a stronger claim that gradual fading is necessary, rather than V5's claim of dependence on data and setup.
